title: Text to speech (TTS): voices, intonation and latency

videos.script: Marginalia wants its phone line to answer with an order's status. That means a machine that speaks. {{title}} Making a voice is the easy part now. Three voices run in this lab, on four ordinary processor cores, faster than they speak. {{voices}} The hard part is everything around the voice. Reading an order number as a number. Reading a date as a date. Saying a Brazilian name in English without mangling it. {{normal}} You will catch those mistakes the way this course catches every mistake. Let the voice speak, and let Whisper write down what it heard. {{roundtrip}} Then you will make the voice ask a question instead of stating one. And you will make it start talking before it has finished thinking. {{latency}} On a phone line, the silence before the first word is the thing people notice most. {{end}}
